points.text: Benchmarks mostly synthetic; real-capture datasets underrepresented.
Robustness to sensor noise, ISP and compression artifacts unclear.
Relies on PSNR/SSIM; lacks perceptual metrics or user study.
Comparisons against task-specialized SOTA per degradation incomplete.
Frozen encoder overfitting or latent collapse not quantitatively analyzed.
Degradation maps and mu-fusion lack quantitative validation.
End-to-end latency and memory at high resolution unreported.
Gap to non-prompt AIR (contrastive embeddings) unclear; incremental integration.
Fairness of encoder pre-training versus baselines' data exposure unclear.
No wall-clock and memory benchmarks to back 85-257x speedup claims.
Unseen tests limited to two combinations; need more OOD types and real captures.
Experimental setting non-standard versus PromptIR/Perceive-IR settings.
Main framework figure confusing.
'Which, where, what' framing lacks convincing evidence.
SupCon pre-training uses degradation labels, contradicting no-prompt claim.
No experiments support the 'which, where, what' motivation.
No benchmarking on unseen task types, only unseen mixtures.
YOLOv12 experiment claimed as contribution but only in supplement.
Citation brackets missing.
PromptIR wrongly described as using manual prompts.
Baseline training protocol and budgets unspecified and apparently unmatched.
Baseline numbers anomalous, suggesting under-trained baselines.
Ablation shows latent prior alone adds little.
Implausible super-additive ablation interaction suggests inconsistent training.
Unclear what replaces latent prior in ablated rows.
'Three times more efficient' and 'fastest' contradicted by Tables 1 and 9.
Unclear whether cost includes frozen VAE encoder.
3WD speedup and memory claims lack data; SA/CA implementation unstated.
Single runs, no variance; small margins.
Splits and checkpoint selection not stated.
'Unseen' cases are combinations of seen degradations.
Out-of-domain results lack baselines.
Table 8 text claims +2.2 dB, table shows at most +0.28.
Table 8 has duplicated cells; appears mis-assembled.
Reported improvements computed against inconsistent baselines.
Inconsistencies: pre-training steps, complexity statements, table references, sign conventions.
'7.40 mAP' gain not reproduced by Table 10.
Code, data and licenses not stated.
Typos and notation mismatch.
PromptIR/DFPIR mischaracterized as manual-prompt methods.
AirNet already learns implicit degradation embeddings; gap overstated.
DAIR uses FFT frequency heuristic it criticizes.
Novelty is combination of known blocks; no AirNet-encoder control.
Claim that encoder captures degradation-specific features untested.
'Unseen' only combinations of seen components.
OOD results lack competitors; gains negligible.
'Reasoning' terminology overstated for gating components.
OneRestore and recent blind AIR methods not compared.
Wrong attributions for SupCon loss and self-attention.
Related-work subsection title mismatched.
Baselines trained with unspecified unmatched budgets; anomalous numbers.
Latent-prior attribution unproven; super-additive with 3WD.
SA/CA variants below base; speed/memory claims without data.
'Without explicit task cues' only at inference; training uses labels.
Manual-prompt characterization of PromptIR/DFPIR questionable.
Table 8 '+2.2 dB' and 'consistently higher' claims contradicted.
Duplicated cells in Table 8.
Efficiency claims contradicted at 512x512.
'Unseen' generalization limited to combinations of seen primitives.
OOD results lack baselines; LPIPS undefined; negligible gains.
Detection evaluation lacks input/clean rows; annotation undocumented; 'first' claim.
mu called global descriptor but is a spatial map.
Table 6 improvement row contradicts caption.
1.68 dB headline is mean of gains against different baselines.
DAEB attention form unspecified; possibly quadratic.
Detection improvement stated against best method only.
'No explicit task cues' claim overstated; pre-training uses labels.
Gain attribution unclear; latent prior alone adds little.
Protocol under-specified: single/multi-task, budgets, splits, selection.
Numerous text-table slips in headline numbers.
No code or reproducibility statement.
Overstated terminology: reasoning, linear attention, unseen.
3WD is a sigmoid gate; comparison to full SA/CA not like-for-like.
Venue fit weak: principle not isolated.
Typos, undefined TS, mixed-baseline improvement row.
Detection lacks degraded-input and clean-reference rows.
Detection test set undocumented; 'first' claim unsupported.
Detector fine-tuning alternative not tried.
Real-world results lack baselines; LPIPS reference undefined; negligible gains.
Efficiency only desktop FP32; no high-res memory or edge numbers.
Degradations outside closed label set (ISP, JPEG, flare) untested.
Behavior under wrong latent code and encoder calibration untested.
Medical use without caution; no broader impact or license.
Table 1 'MP' column undefined.

P.summary: Benchmarks mostly synthetic; real captures underrepresented.
Generalization to genuinely unseen degradation types untested.
Only PSNR/SSIM; no perceptual or user study.
End-to-end latency and memory unreported; speedups unsubstantiated.
Degradation labels used despite no-prompt claim.

Q.summary: Baseline training protocol unspecified and unmatched.
Efficiency claims contradicted by own tables.
3WD speed/memory claims lack data and implementation.
'Unseen' limited to combinations of seen degradations.
OOD/real-world results lack baselines; weak gains.
Modest novelty versus AirNet-style embeddings; no control.
Method uses the frequency heuristic it criticizes.
OneRestore and recent blind AIR not compared.
Degradation labels used despite no-cue claim.
Detection evaluation lacks references and documentation.
Efficiency measured only on desktop; no high-res memory.
